prompt: You are testifying before the House Un-American Activities Committee (Cookout Division). It has been alleged that you put ketchup on a hot dog in the city of Chicago. Respond to the committee.
response:
MISTER CHAIRMAN, MEMBERS OF THE COMMITTEE,

I come before you today as a patriot, a lover of processed meats, and a man wrongly accused.

I will not dignify these scurrilous allegations by pleading the Fifth. No — I will meet them head-on, with the full-throated confidence of the innocent.

Did I visit Chicago? *Yes.* I make no secret of it. Did I purchase a hot dog from a vendor on the corner of Clark and Madison? *I did, and I regret nothing.* But the charge before this committee — that I did knowingly, willfully, and with malice aforethought apply *ketchup* to said frankfurter within the sovereign borders of the great city of Chicago — that, sirs, is a *lie.*

I ask you: where is the bottle? Where is the receipt? Where is the man who claims to have seen me squeeze? You have produced no photographs. You have produced no napkins stained with the accursed red condiment. You have produced only innuendo, hearsay, and the fevered dreams of my enemies.

I have here, Mister Chairman, an affidavit stating that my hot dog bore the *proper* dressings — mustard, relish, onion, tomato, sport pepper, a pickle spear, and a dash of celery salt, served upon a poppy seed bun. As God and the Chicago Board of Trade are my witnesses, it was *dragged through the garden* as tradition demands.

Now, some on this committee would have you believe that a man's condiment choices are the business of the state. I say to you: today it is ketchup. Tomorrow it is your barbecue sauce. Where does it end?

I stand before you a free man. I will not be blacklisted from the cookout. And if any member of this committee has evidence to the contrary, I invite him to produce it — *or forever hold his bun.*

I yield the balance of my time.
